jordan: Heads-up: I ran the latest kernel selector on v2 models and saw a ~7-10% p99 latency regression under our replay harness. Need a harmonized head-to-head to rule out tokenizer/decoding differences. Anyone able to help? :eyes:

ravi: Can you paste the exact harness command you used? Was batching forced or dynamic? Any KV cache warmup differences?

jordan: Here’s the command I used:
```
bench-run --mode=replay --seed=stable --models="modelA,modelB" \
  --align-tokenizer=true --decode="temp=0.0,top_p=0.95,stop=[\"\n\",\"END\"]" \
  --batching=auto --kv-warmup=full --stream=true --out=~/runs/1812345678
```

mia: Two quick checks: ensure tokenizer vocab mapping is identical (we once had a shifted mapping), and compare initial prefix length distribution. Also set `--stream=false` to avoid subtle buffering effects from the runtime.

jordan: Good call. Re-ran with `--tokenizer-map=canonical` and `--stream=false`. New results: modelA p95 220ms -> 235ms, modelB p95 215ms -> 217ms. p99 deltas are worse (up to ~10%). bench-bot, attach profile pls.

bench-bot: Profile upload: https://ci.redwood/infer/profiles/1812345678. Summary: kernel_selector: +12% time attributed to attention_kernel_v2, batching_utilization down ~8% due to smaller effective batch sizes after selector change. KV cache hit rate unchanged.

lena: If batching_utilization dropped, maybe continuous batching heuristics were tightened; did the selector add a stricter cutoff for small sequence paths? Also check async memcpy overhead on the new kernel.

ravi: I can reproduce with synthetic traffic too. Synthetic mixed short/long reqs shows similar p99 blip. My hypothesis: selector now prefers attn_v2 for long seqs but picks it for short seqs too because estimated throughput favors it, and that kernel has higher fixed overhead for short sequences.

mia: We should run an aligned comparison: same rand seed, same prompt set, identical stop sequences, force canonical tokenizer mapping, and explicitly set all decode params. Also capture allocation traces and kernel-selection logs. Can we run `--force-kernel=attn_v1` vs `--force-kernel=attn_v2`?

jordan: Agree. Proposed plan:
1) baseline: old kernel (attn_v1) with canonical tokenizer, full KV warmup.
2) new selector default (attn_v2 picks).
3) new selector but force batching thresholds to previous values.
Collect p50/p95/p99, allocation/trace, kernel selection logs, and tokenization diffs for each run. I’ll kick these off and post CSVs.

bench-bot: Started jobs 1812345678-1, 1812345678-2, 1812345678-3. ETA ~25m. Will upload summarized CSV to the same CI bucket.

ravi: Also add `--kv-preload=none` to see cold-cache behavior; our full warmup runs might be masking latency cliffs.

jordan: Adding `--kv-preload=none` for one of the runs. Thanks. If anyone has a quick tokenization diff script, drop it here.

mia: Tiny script to dump token ids for prompts:
```
python3 - <<EOF
from tokenizers import Tokenizer
t=Tokenizer.from_file('canonical.json')
for s in open('prompts.txt'):
    print(t.encode(s.strip()).ids)
EOF
```

lena: :thumbsup: will review results and the kernel selection traces once bench-bot posts the CSVs.

jordan: Thanks all — will update in this thread when the runs finish and attach the perf diffs and allocation traces.
